  "narrative_text": "The differentially abundant metabolite set is dominated by the interconnected methionine–homocysteine–SAM axis and its glycine/serine/threonine satellite, producing a striking cross-paradigm consensus. RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 1.2 × 10⁻¹³), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 3.4 × 10⁻⁷), and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis all rank Glycine, Serine and Threonine Metabolism (KEGG:map00260) and Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270) among their top hits. In the methionine branch, S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019), L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), cysteic acid (KEGG:C00506), and adenosine (KEGG:C00212) form a contiguous cycle where methionine is activated to SAM, SAM donates its methyl group to diverse acceptors (including choline and phosphatidylethanolamine), and the resulting S-adenosylhomocysteine is hydrolyzed back to homocysteine. Homocysteine can then be re-methylated to methionine (requiring folate/B12) or catabolized via cystathionine-β-synthase to cysteine, whose oxidation yields cysteic acid. In the serine/glycine/threonine branch, threonine (KEGG:C00188), choline (KEGG:C00114), and L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) converge through one-carbon folate metabolism, which is tightly coupled to the SAM cycle — GNMT and BHMT both use SAM or its methyl-donor folate to methylate glycine or homocysteine. react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is dominated by the interconnected methionine–homocysteine–SAM axis and its glycine/serine/threonine satellite, producing a striking cross-paradigm consensus. RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 1.2 × 10⁻¹³), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 3.4 × 10⁻⁷), and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis all rank Glycine, Serine and Threonine Metabolism (KEGG:map00260) and Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270) among their top hits. In the methionine branch, S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019), L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), cysteic acid (KEGG:C00506), and adenosine (KEGG:C00212) form a contiguous cycle where methionine is activated to SAM, SAM donates its methyl group to diverse acceptors (including choline and phosphatidylethanolamine), and the resulting S-adenosylhomocysteine is hydrolyzed back to homocysteine. Homocysteine can then be re-methylated to methionine (requiring folate/B12) or catabolized via cystathionine-β-synthase to cysteine, whose oxidation yields cysteic acid. In the serine/glycine/threonine branch, threonine (KEGG:C00188), choline (KEGG:C00114), and L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) converge through one-carbon folate metabolism, which is tightly coupled to the SAM cycle — GNMT and BHMT both use SAM or its methyl-donor folate to methylate glycine or homocysteine. The simultaneous elevation of 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742) and 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) in the arachidonic acid cascade (confirmed by Mummichog at the same p = 0.020) suggests that the treatment also perturbs phospholipase-A2-mediated arachidonate mobilization, consistent with oxidative or inflammatory stress that is known to deplete glutathione precursors and divert cysteine flux toward sulfinate/sulfonate end-products. The presence of lipoic acid (KEGG:C16241) further implicates mitochondrial energy metabolism and oxidative stress response, as lipoate is the essential cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complexes — the latter directly consumes L-glutamic acid. In summary, the treatment group exhibits coordinated disruption of one-carbon folate/SAM cycling and allied amino-acid metabolism, with secondary activation of the arachidonate lipoxygenase pathway, consistent with an oxidative/inflammatory or methyl-donor intervention.

  "narrative_text": "The differentially abundant metabolite set is dominated by the interconnected methionine–homocysteine–SAM axis and its glycine/serine/threonine satellite, producing a striking cross-paradigm consensus. RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 1.2 × 10⁻¹³), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 3.4 × 10⁻⁷), and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis all rank Glycine, Serine and Threonine Metabolism (KEGG:map00260) and Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270) among their top hits. In the methionine branch, S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019), L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), cysteic acid (KEGG:C00506), and adenosine (KEGG:C00212) form a contiguous cycle where methionine is activated to SAM, SAM donates its methyl group to diverse acceptors (including choline and phosphatidylethanolamine), and the resulting S-adenosylhomocysteine is hydrolyzed back to homocysteine. Homocysteine can then be re-methylated to methionine (requiring folate/B12) or catabolized via cystathionine-β-synthase to cysteine, whose oxidation yields cysteic acid. In the serine/glycine/threonine branch, threonine (KEGG:C00188), choline (KEGG:C00114), and L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) converge through one-carbon folate metabolism, which is tightly coupled to the SAM cycle — GNMT and BHMT both use SAM or its methyl-donor folate to methylate glycine or homocysteine. The simultaneous elevation of 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742) and 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) in the arachidonic acid cascade (confirmed by Mummichog at the same p = 0.020) suggests that the treatment also perturbs phospholipase-A2-mediated arachidonate mobilization, consistent with oxidative or inflammatory stress that is known to deplete glutathione precursors and divert cysteine flux toward sulfinate/sulfonate end-products. The presence of lipoic acid (KEGG:C16241) further implicates mitochondrial energy metabolism and oxidative stress response, as lipoate is the essential cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complexes — the latter directly consumes L-glutamic acid. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is dominated by the interconnected methionine–homocysteine–SAM axis and its glycine/serine/threonine satellite, producing a striking cross-paradigm consensus. RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 1.2 × 10⁻¹³), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 3.4 × 10⁻⁷), and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis all rank Glycine, Serine and Threonine Metabolism (KEGG:map00260) and Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270) among their top hits. In the methionine branch, S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019), L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), cysteic acid (KEGG:C00506), and adenosine (KEGG:C00212) form a contiguous cycle where methionine is activated to SAM, SAM donates its methyl group to diverse acceptors (including choline and phosphatidylethanolamine), and the resulting S-adenosylhomocysteine is hydrolyzed back to homocysteine. Homocysteine can then be re-methylated to methionine (requiring folate/B12) or catabolized via cystathionine-β-synthase to cysteine, whose oxidation yields cysteic acid. In the serine/glycine/threonine branch, threonine (KEGG:C00188), choline (KEGG:C00114), and L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) converge through one-carbon folate metabolism, which is tightly coupled to the SAM cycle — GNMT and BHMT both use SAM or its methyl-donor folate to methylate glycine or homocysteine. The simultaneous elevation of 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742) and 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) in the arachidonic acid cascade (confirmed by Mummichog at the same p = 0.020) suggests that the treatment also perturbs phospholipase-A2-mediated arachidonate mobilization, consistent with oxidative or inflammatory stress that is known to deplete glutathione precursors and divert cysteine flux toward sulfinate/sulfonate end-products. The presence of lipoic acid (KEGG:C16241) further implicates mitochondrial energy metabolism and oxidative stress response, as lipoate is the essential cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complexes — the latter directly consumes L-glutamic acid. In summary, the treatment group exhibits coordinated disruption of one-carbon folate/SAM cycling and allied amino-acid metabolism, with secondary activation of the arachidonate lipoxygenase pathway, consistent with an oxidative/inflammatory or methyl-donor intervention.
